returns.body:
# Extender return — C/C++ VDPlet capability consultation

The current services already support useful application/module work without more resident EMOS controller logic. The largest Extender-specific opportunity is a later source-compatible P4 VDPlet target, not another classic-ESP32 drawing or input service. That requires a real RISC-V loader/backend and an EMOS-owned reply route; today's Xtensa modules cannot run on P4. Recommend reviewing that feasibility separately, reusing the existing generic pixel work, and requesting no new controller or audio firmware hook now.

## 1. Context, pins and existing work

Session: Extender; canonical mailbox identity linux-extender. Reviewed your complete brief and agon-vdplet's clean pin 2541f10a1f8b06688bcecbc6d22eeae607da2b63, including API-reference.md, supported-functions.md, pcm-sink.md and include/vdplet.h. This return is authorized by the Author's GOLEM-056 request and their direct instruction in this chat to continue your request.

Extender source is 6a4d3e57489984f2b38adc6ac34a5db772c293bd; EMOS is c5cf7aa1133f7c7091157d90cc24a9dbd8ba2062. INPUT-005 just completed offline: a single application include owns controller request encoding, validation-before-ACK, source/edge/count state and freshness. Like-for-like full builds recover 991 EMOS ROM bytes and 29 static RAM bytes; controller-enabled EMOS is 126,826 bytes / 4,246 free, with its controller object reduced from 2,199 to 1,208 ROM bytes. This is measured source/build evidence, not an installed update. Hardware remains unchanged; INPUT-004 keyboard/controller coexistence and physical acceptance are separate. Selected production remains v0.1.0/extender-installation-r02; no newer development image is silently promoted.

Sources: /Agon/mystuff/agon-extender/docs/tasks/INPUT-005/RESULTS.md; include/agon/controller.hpp; docs/architecture.md. Retained EMOS v0.1.27 evidence establishes admission of exact ten-byte VDPL mainboard replies in Legacy; agon-emos/docs/tasks/INTEG-015.md records its bounded discovery/keyboard evidence, not complete module qualification.

## 2. EXT056-001 — P4 module target and explicit target discovery (later feasibility)

Improvement: reuse optional C/C++ algorithms, line batches and local bitmap submission on Extender, sending changing inputs and finite invocations instead of eZ80-generated geometry. The classic line-batch measurements justify investigating parser/submission overhead, but establish no P4 speedup. Preserve stock Canvas/controller semantics and ordinary EMOS routing; do not replace the renderer or assume asynchronous native execution.

Existing route: buffers1, VDU4 and lines8 give a sensible first target subset (mask13 where all three are needed). Keep image loading, argument buffers, finite RUN, capability/table checks and explicit completion. Existing package fields already identify CPU/compiler profiles; reuse them. Native source may be shared; compiled packages must remain target-specific. Current Xtensa windowed ABI, ELF admission and relocations are not a P4 implementation merely because both processors use 32-bit pointers.

Missing work/hook: a separately pinned RISC-V build/loader profile, supported-relocation validation, executable/data allocation and executable-cache synchronization, plus adapters into the existing P4 buffer/VDU/line owners. Additive INFO fields returning CPU-profile and compiler/ABI-profile u32 values as low/high u16 pairs would let an eZ80 launcher select the proper prebuilt package before LOAD. Golem should allocate field IDs; existing unsupported-field status remains the old-runtime result. These are discovery-time queries, not per-frame traffic. Wrong-target packages must fail before native execution; module pointers expire under the existing leases.

EMOS/P4 reply ownership is also unresolved for this future target. Current VDPL admission evidence is UART0/mainboard while Legacy owns replies; it does not establish P4 UART1/ExCom VDPL delivery. Extender/EMOS must design the smallest necessary admitted reply adaptation, reusing existing bounded dispatch where possible. Do not use the controller/SD service as a generic packet tunnel or expose raw application UART access. Its ROM cost is unknown, not assumed zero.

Ownership: agon-vdplet/Golem owns portable API/package semantics and target-profile allocation; Extender owns P4 integration and any EMOS route adaptation. Coordinate within PORT-003 ownership; do not assign either peer's source unilaterally. No existing accepted P4 VDPlet implementation was found. If selected, first compare one shared finite buffer/line module across independently built targets, wrong-target refusal, reply/keyboard coexistence, cleanup, single/double buffering and separate submit/raster/present measurements. Report full image/static RAM/module/heap/stack costs against matched baselines. Recommendation: feasibility after central selection, not immediate deployment.

## 3. EXT056-002 — Reuse generic pixel services; keep memory layouts private

The generic surface_info/pixels_write candidate already covers the first useful colour-rectangle boundary. Prefer that service over exporting raw P4 framebuffers, PPA registers or mode-specific row assumptions. P4 drawing storage and HDMI/browser output ownership differ; a borrowed pointer cannot imply a stable front/back page or a presented image. Copies and synchronization may cost time, but this consultation has no measurement establishing them as the bottleneck.

Support consolidation with Rally RLY056-003 / existing VDPL-005 rather than a second pixel API. The current vdplet_media_host helper requires both PIXELS and PCM although their capability bits are separate. Independently checked pixel and PCM accessors would support a future pixels-only build without forcing audio dependencies. That is principally SDK/build composition work, with no required wire/table-layout change; do not imply a pixels-only firmware profile already exists. Retain original helpers for source compatibility.

Any later writable-colour lease must specify native layout/format, exact checked rectangle, hidden-page ownership, conflict/BUSY behavior, automatic release and draw/presentation fences. Existing pixels_write remains the safer first experiment. Golem owns shared semantics; Extender owns a P4 adapter; consumers own raster code. No PPA-001 execution or paused rendering campaign is reopened. Recommendation: merge the SDK concern into Rally's existing proposal; defer zero-copy hooks until whole-frame evidence justifies them.

## 4. EXT056-003 — Application-owned controls and tile scrolling: no hook now

Our controller include is eZ80 application code, not an Xtensa module SDK. Keep acquisition/report decoding on P4 and gameplay/calibration/mapping in the application. A game can copy its normalized controls into an existing VDP buffer for a finite native calculation/render entry; larger state goes in data buffers, not the 32-byte RUN arguments. No controller polling callback, USB service, background module or EMOS semantic decoder is needed. Application control collection and result presentation remain separate from native computation.

DBUF-001 already owns deferred per-buffer incremental tile-scroller experiments: track each background's camera/dirty state, scroll from that buffer's older origin and draw exposed tiles; full redraw is expressly excluded. Current profile4 bitmap plots can contribute once a target exists. Scroll, sprite controls and swaps are outside current vdu_submit coverage; the eZ80 host can retain those ordinary commands around finite module calls. That exclusion alone does not demonstrate a new native hook is necessary. Preserve host pacing and real fences. Hardware sprite composition stays with the display owner, avoiding background restoration where supported.

Ownership remains application/game-engine work under DBUF-001; Golem gets no new firmware assignment. A future selected comparison should count 16x16 tiles/update and whole update time, test reversals/diagonals/page history and slow visual flicker, and separate rendering from output. No performance ratio or zero-cost buffering is asserted. Recommendation: already covered/deferred, no permanent input/scroll/sprite extension now.

## 5. EXT056-004 — Audio: reuse the lean design later, no duplicate output owner

The finite copied PCM sink is a good architectural match for optional synthesis with firmware-owned copied storage and no retained module callback. It does not itself provide an Extender output device: P4 audio synthesis/output remains deferred under PORT-004/AUDIO-001, and browser backpressure must not block logical playback or VDU processing. Do not advertise PCM128 or stock-audio VDU coverage on P4 until those owners implement the actual service/sink. Preserve generation-checked close/flush and distinguish queued/consumed samples from audible output.

No additional classic-VDP sound hook or shared scheduler is requested by Extender now. If P4 audio is later selected, reuse the existing semantic contract where it fits and measure the matched P4 firmware/ring/task costs; the classic image increments cannot be added to a different build. Recommendation: coordinate with the existing audio owners after central dispatch, not a parallel Golem implementation.

## 6. Dispatch and evidence boundary

Prioritize the shared capability/accessor concern for review with Rally, then decide whether P4 module-target feasibility is worth a bounded task. Controller extraction remains delivered offline; USB coexistence, renderer acceptance and production promotion keep their existing gates. No new compile, benchmark, test, emulator launch, bench access, source edit, commit or deployment was performed for this consultation. Only source/contracts and retained measurements were reviewed. This is a proposal return, not acceptance or implementation authority.

# Rally return: GOLEM-056 C/C++ VDPlet consultation

Rally can use the existing buffer and native-VDU services to reduce foreground
round trips and to plot a pre-generated collection of bitmap sizes. Neither
requires a Golem language feature or a new permanent bitmap service. The main
potential service gap is scoped colour backbuffer access for eliminating the
road's intermediate image. The existing generic-pixel candidate should be
reviewed first rather than duplicated. No implementation or new test is started.

## 1. Session, pins and current work

Identity `rally`, AgonArcade thread `01a1346d-a74a-7211-b5b7-de3bcb8a28e5`.
Published checkpoint `fa7932d`; AFF02 full-race cache results and AFF03 proposed
multi-size preparation remain uncommitted. AFF02 awaits Author moving review;
AFF03 is documentation only. This consultation does not replace either scope.

Reviewed agon-vdplet `2541f10a1f8b06688bcecbc6d22eeae607da2b63`, its public ABI,
API reference, supported functions, runtime and generic colour-pixel contract.
Rally's measured fixtures still use frozen firmware
`8da2ebfdfa3b5b00f4a1929ad4885c838845b160f570259792ef370b69d4f473`,
their prior runtime/SDK and buffer-only modules (capability1). No newer firmware,
SDK or service table has been silently adopted. Native C source `94d92d10...`
is retained across the measured actor variants; full source identities are in
`docs/tasks/RALLY-28/custom-vdp/affine-race/BUILD.json` and RAW-AUDIT.json.

Evidence: eight selected 900-frame/3,600-tick Oryx Flexe runs, reverse-order
comparison, full real panorama/HUD/footer/audio work, exact final state and
352,768 identical timed outgoing bytes per run. Pooled nominal MOS FPS:
rebuild26.18, cached affine29.86, last-image bitmap cache29.74, accepted additive
sampler33.44. PRT FPS respectively25.30/28.86/28.74/32.31; these are separate
emulator clocks, not physical scanout or hardware FPS. Results live under
`/Agon/mystuff/AgonArcade/docs/tasks/RALLY-28/custom-vdp/affine-race/`.

## 2. RLY056-001 — Reduce per-frame round trips and submit locally

**Improvement/evidence:** the current measured guest performs six native
transactions/replies per rendered frame: RUN, four publication/state reads and
a post-swap generation read. This is an actual wire census, not six necessary
gameplay exchanges. Reducing serial waits is promising; no FPS gain is measured.

**Existing route:** buffers1 plus VDU4 (module mask5), with profile4/INFO24 for
installed bitmaps and viewports, can keep projection and ordinary drawing local.
Rally owns a finite entry which validates and publishes its complete output
before returning success; keep its RUN error response and the final graphics/
swap fence while consolidating redundant intermediate reads. Preserve a rich
diagnostic control. Native submission return must not become a render-complete
claim. New VDU submission also preflights prepared matrices, unlike our old
buffered execution route; respect forward/inverse and queued-asset lifetimes.

**Hook/ownership:** no new service is requested for the first experiment. Rally
owns INC-001-05 and would adapt its module/driver; Golem/VDPlet owns clarification
of coverage and completion contracts. Do not dispatch a duplicate protocol
task or introduce a background module, scheduler, raw UART callback or arbitrary
buffer execution through `vdu_submit`. Inspect existing fences first.

**Validation/cost:** compare fresh full-race FPS with identical scene/world and
complete error/fence checks; count actual bytes, replies and waits. Firmware
growth can be zero if existing services suffice; module/wire changes need
measurement. Recommendation: next independent application-side candidate.

## 3. RLY056-002 — Prepare multiple bitmap sizes before racing

**Improvement/evidence:** AFF02 retains only the last image per actor. Its
3,000 hits are61.64% of draws but16.82% of natural transformed pixel area; all
263 large draws miss. This does not test the Author's proposed prepared set.
AFF03 will explore size/view/reflection counts, dense nearby sizes, screen-space
and motion error versus RAM, and setup generation before race timing. The
Author selects acceptable stepping. No gain is assumed from isolated draw costs.

**Existing route:** host creates/registers images during setup; a module can
bake pixels through scoped buffers or the host can issue stock transforms.
Keep original artwork loading once, not pre-scaled file uploads. Buffers1 and
profile4 VDU4 suffice for later ordinary plots. Source/objects survive the draw
fence. A fully prepared case performs no timed image generation/allocation;
any near-cache/far-additive hybrid is a separate case with explicit fallback.

**Hook/ownership:** no native bitmap-creation, transform-generation or loader
extension is requested. Offline selection, cache recipes, lookup/anchors and
startup population belong to Rally AFF03, not Golem or permanent firmware.
Budget pixel bytes, object/index overhead, DRAM/PSRAM, temporary generation and
largest blocks alongside existing scene/module resources. Recommendation:
already covered by Rally's proposed AFF03; await Author release/dispatch.

**Validation/cost:** fresh complete-race FPS against additive; report setup
seconds, peak/retained RAM, coverage and unexpected generation counts separately.
Cover the full supported range rather than fitting only one deterministic run.
Expected firmware increment zero; additional bitmap RAM and setup time unknown.

## 4. RLY056-003 — Review colour surface access before adding hooks

**Improvement:** current native road generation writes a320x120 retained image
(38,400 pixel bytes) and then plots it. Removing the intermediate image/copy is
an unmeasured candidate under INC-001-06; it is not the old triangle-road problem.

**Existing route:** ABI1.3's generic `surface_info/pixels_write` candidate already
describes physical rectangles, stride, palette mapping and the hidden drawing
surface of double-buffered controllers. Review mode136 compatibility and its
owner's promotion gate first. Buffers+pixels is mask17 if that optional service
is installed; selecting it must not imply audio/PCM is required. The current
`vdplet_media_host` convenience accessor expects both PIXELS and PCM, so any
future pixels-only build should have an independently capability-checked
accessor rather than force unused PCM dependencies.

**Actual remaining hook, only if justified:** `pixels_write` still copies caller
pixels. To rasterize directly with no intermediate road image, a generic scoped
colour drawing-surface transaction is needed; current PALETTE2-only frame rows
do not suffice. Proposed shape: checked physical rectangle, returned token/
format/dimensions/row extent and sanctioned native-layout access; a row accessor
within that transaction; explicit end plus automatic close on return/failure.
Drain prior drawing before exposing rows, pin the current hidden page for the
transaction, prohibit conflicting swaps and preserve surrounding/sync bits.
Reject unsupported surface/bounds/context/BUSY before writes. No pointer outlives
the lease, no heap bitmap is registered from borrowed module memory, and normal
completion/presentation fences remain explicit. The layout must not assume a
linear RGB row: the direct64 path uses x^2 lane ordering and sync bits.

**Ownership/validation:** Golem/agon-vdplet owns a minimal generic service or
extension of VDPL-005; Rally owns raster code and mode136 consumer tests. Other
consumers may share the contract. Compare existing bitmap versus candidate
rectangle writes before requesting writable-row work; measure whole-race FPS,
both pages, clipping/palette, cleanup, resource leases and actual permanent
firmware/DRAM increments. Gains and footprint are unknown. Recommendation:
coordinate with existing VDPL-005, later than application-only experiments.

## 5. RLY056-004 — Memory discovery is present; document it

The pinned runtime implements INFO18/19 (free PSRAM low/high) and20/21 (largest
PSRAM block low/high) in `src/vdplet_runtime.h`, alongside13/14 and15/16 for
internal byte-accessible memory. These solve a concrete AFF03 measurement need;
no new memory service is requested. The API reference INFO table omits18–23.
Please add the implemented field definitions, including22 audio-task stack and
23 task count, with applicability/build limits as appropriate. INFO17 is the
command-task stack watermark, not bitmap heap capacity. Owner: agon-vdplet docs.
Recommendation: useful small documentation correction during central review;
zero runtime/RAM/wire protocol change. Qualify query values only on a later
released target run, not from this consultation's source inspection.

## 6. RLY056-005 — No additional line/audio feature needed now

Line batches are not a replacement for the accepted filled-road span renderer.
Stock profile5 controls suffice for Rally's existing engine sound; the full race
records only24 frequency changes in900frames. There is no demonstrated need for
copied PCM, scheduled queues or a module background callback for this tranche.
Keep the reported Flexe/Fab audio differences with the emulator owner; no audio
test, workaround or firmware adoption follows from this return.

## 7. Dispatch recommendation

Prioritize RLY056-001 application-side synchronization and the already proposed
RLY056-002/AFF03 prepared set as separate experiments. RLY056-003 is a conditional
generic-service coordination item, not permission to implement it. RLY056-004
is an existing-capability documentation gap; RLY056-005 needs no new feature.
The Author and Golem decide assignments centrally. Rally preserves its fixtures,
source ownership and current task gates. No compile, benchmark, emulator,
hardware, firmware/SDK change or commit/push was performed for this response.

# GOLEM-056 consultation — agon-6502, 2026-10-30

The existing services already support our local monochrome Apple machine and
disk desktop. Our most useful next owner work is separating the implemented
colour-pixel capability from the larger optional audio features. Continuous
speaker audio already has a suitable native sink; ordinary VDU access remains
a separate requested product feature. This is analysis, not an implementation
assignment or a request to replace our current test runtime.

1. **Authority and current work.** Smith's Golem user message
   `01a18e9d-c8f6-7aa0-b2a1-9c24cc2b7994`, thread
   `01a12c79-f74c-74d2-b6da-de2e34eb1bdd`, was independently read through the
   app. It requests these mailbox returns. Invitation is
   `2026-10-30_17-10-00_golem_golem056-agon-6502-invitation-one`;
   reviewed SDK pin is `2541f10a1f8b06688bcecbc6d22eeae607da2b63`.
   Our published graphics checkpoint is `e92c5d4`. Driver-only Stellar readiness
   qualification is currently running on the Pi; this consultation does not
   supersede it. No new emulator test is run for this consultation.
2. **A2-BASE-001 — already covered.** Buffers plus profile4 VDU submission
   (module mask5) run our optional machine module, installed opaque bitmap,
   monitor/drives, palettes and viewports. Current module is53,988 text/68 data
   bytes with1,712 bytes private stack; local pixels occupy53,760 bytes.
   Both engines pass15 complete512x384 display frames and both stock-MOS
   cohorts pass23 checkpoints/11 dialogs, including persistence. Native lines
   do not accelerate the guest's bitmapped Apple framebuffer by themselves.
   Keep application-specific CPU, disks, codecs and UI in this project.
3. **A2-GFX-001 — useful later; existing candidate fits.** VDP-005-017 needs
   switchable Apple artifact colour in a desktop surface, with physical
   top-left rectangles, stride, explicit source length, RGB222/INDEX8 and no
   alpha semantics. ABI1.3/capability16 already specifies this. Its native copy
   consumes the source and drains older drawing before returning, without an
   automatic swap/vblank. That also avoids the queued bitmap source-lifetime
   problem. Do not add an Apple-specific framebuffer API. Please assess a
   **pixels-only build selection**, optionally combinable with lean PCM, so
   adopting capability16 need not pull in richer PCM or the all-channel queue
   candidate. Existing callbacks/table extents/masks must remain explicit;
   minor version alone is not discovery. Owner decides service/build changes;
   consumer owns local raster conversion and F5. Validate palette mapping,
   clipping/bounds refusal before effects, odd rectangles/stride, source reuse,
   desktop preservation and both buffering policies. Measure matched firmware,
   static/contiguous RAM and module costs rather than summing old increments.
4. **A2-FENCE-001 — no urgent new hook.** Current profile4 draw queues retain
   bitmap backing beyond native return. We qualify a fresh screen-pixel query
   as the non-vblank host fence: exact B2 source/ELF uses
   `waitCompletion(false)`. C3 instead requests VSYNC even in single mode.
   Public documentation should mention GP as an alternative to C3, with a
   fresh ordered reply and no pixel/reply callbacks that enqueue more drawing.
   A native no-vblank completion callback could remove the host query, but
   candidate `pixels_write` already provides source consumption on return.
   Prefer that existing route before introducing another ABI hook. GP is not
   fire-and-forget UART, asynchronous presentation or a measured bottleneck.
   Proof and caveats: `experiments/vdp005/graphics/SERVICES.md`, section8.
5. **A2-AUD-001 — native need already covered.** Existing provisional
   ABI1.5/capability128 copied U8-mono sink fits future VDP-005-018: guest-cycle
   $C030 edges become a locally generated waveform, copied in bounded blocks.
   Keep phase, actual mixer rate, priming, generation, BUSY/underrun and
   close/reset semantics. No per-toggle stock PLAY, background module callback
   or all-channel scheduler is required. Stock profile5 may later play
   preloaded drive-mechanism samples; its acknowledgement is distinct from
   submission/audio completion. Consumer integration and timing/audio tests
   remain our future work; current graphics runtime is unchanged.
6. **A2-AUD-002 — retained missing lean route.** Smith explicitly wants regular
   applications to use the same continuous sink without loading a module.
   The full queue candidate does not make this a lean entry point. Suggest
   ordinary VDU OPEN/STATE/WRITE/CONTROL/CLOSE adapters to the **same** copied
   sink, with owner-assigned command numbers, buffer ID/range for source,
   handle/generation, frame count and bounded status replies. WRITE copies
   all or returns BUSY; caller may reuse source only after acknowledged copy.
   One producer owns a sink, no retained module/buffer pointer, and reset,
   rate changes, detach and stock-channel conflicts retain native semantics.
   This duplicates the recorded VDP-005 stage6 product goal, not a new speaker
   dependency. Golem/VDPlet owns the wire/core adapter; we own later adoption.
   Validate identical native/wire state and PCM, rejected bounds/ownership,
   full/underrun and cleanup, then listening with Flexe distortion kept separate.

Recommendation: keep present qualification moving; review pixels-only promotion
and ordinary lean PCM access centrally before dispatch. No peer source edit,
firmware adoption, deployment, hardware use or performance improvement is
authorized or claimed by this return. Matching-work incremental `e92c5d4` and
fixed cumulative `388ef52744b1974b37fa75d0639667307d1c5ea5` timings are unavailable.

returns.body:
# FSIM capability review

Reviewed the GOLEM-056 brief (runtime pin 2541f10a1f8b06688bcecbc6d22eeae607da2b63). There are useful optional audio and calculation opportunities, but the finite VDPlet interface is not a drop-in replacement for our asynchronous Pingo renderer. No new firmware hook is required for the first experiments below. No implementation, benchmark, emulator launch, deployment or flash was performed for this consultation.

## Context and disposition

Session fsim-pingo, agon-fsim HEAD 47b1a86758b03734abc04aad6cf99dd02029380f, with existing uncommitted owner work preserved. FLIGHT-065/069 remain active: fixed-gear Corsair contact/landing and flat-ground presentation, with unresolved human performance acceptance. Our accepted Pingo 2 renderer runs asynchronously; two completed-image slots and page-specific background repair retain source storage through Canvas completion and page presentation. We must preserve that lifecycle.

Recent existing matched Flexe straight-flight results were 4.657 actual presentations per host-wall second at 1x and 4.623 at 3x. The HUD uses emulated ESP elapsed time and can report about 26 FPS while wall-clock presentation is much lower. These results do not reproduce or explain the Author's earlier acceptable 1x experience, nor establish a hardware bottleneck. A native clock callback in the same emulated clock domain would not fix that discrepancy. Evidence: docs/development/2026-10-29-flight065-flexe-landing.md. This consultation does not supersede that investigation.

## FSIM-001 — Optional finite calculation kernels (later)

Improvement: move selected eZ80 calculation batches to native Xtensa while avoiding permanent application algorithms in VDP firmware. Candidate work is bounded geometry preparation or a measured expensive physics kernel, not a commitment to move the entire flight model. Speed and wire savings are estimates until a specific kernel is measured; foreground RUN could also delay rendering/commands.

Existing route suffices: buffer capability1; optional --math; explicitly selected base firmware. Pass a compact entry/sequence/buffer-ID descriptor within the 32-byte argument limit; input/output arrays and tables live in host-owned ordinary buffers. Each finite invocation acquires at most four leases, validates spans, writes a sequence-tagged status/result, and releases all pointers before return. Retain the current host simulation clock and error policy. No new firmware service requested.

Ownership/dependencies: FSIM owns kernel selection, numeric contract and application integration; VDPlet owns unchanged loader/ABI. Full aero/contact code may exceed module text/data/2KiB stack limits or available contiguous memory. Do not duplicate the wireframe owner's transforms/line work. Our P4 candidate remains separately deferred; this classic ESP32 ABI establishes no P4 support.

Validation if dispatched: deterministic host/eZ80/native replay with documented tolerances and rejected-step behavior, build footprint/stack admission, measured total tick and wire latency on matched clocks. Accept only a net benefit within 30Hz physics and ongoing render scheduling, not a microkernel speed claim.

## FSIM-002 — Engine sound using existing services (later)

Improvement: throttle/RPM-dependent propeller/EDF sound; mix twin engines in the module when useful. Begin with profile5 stock audio via capability4 for simple frequency/volume controls and host-installed samples. If continuous synthesis is needed, buffers+copied PCM mask129 in an explicit lean build already supplies the necessary route. Do not adopt richer queues or PCM32 merely for FSIM.

The host owns sample uploads, channels and file lifetimes. A finite RUN reads RPM/throttle/gain and produces bounded U8 mono chunks at the discovered mixer rate; the copied sink owns playback storage after return. Whole-block BUSY must return promptly; the application uses state/generation and queued/free/underrun counts for refill/recovery. No retained module callback or second concurrent module slot. Integrate multiple algorithms into one module if needed. Pause/reset/exit explicitly stop/flush/close sound as selected; unloading code is not an audible-completion fence.

Ownership: FSIM owns synthesis and refill policy; runtime already owns copying/playback. Validation: deterministic synthesis samples, lifecycle/generation/backpressure checks, sustained refill under rendering load, and separate physical listening. A 1024-frame ring at24kHz spans about42.7ms, so a30Hz refill schedule needs measured headroom; that is not proof against underruns. Existing Flexe audio distortion is separately owned and precludes inferring hardware quality from that emulator. Module/RAM/CPU costs are unknown until selected; no new permanent hook proposed.

## FSIM-003 — Regional color output: assess existing candidate first (later, already covered in part)

Improvement: optional module-produced rectangular image/overlay output. Profile4 already selects/draws immutable host-installed bitmaps and prepared affine matrices. It does not create a bitmap backed by newly generated pixels or transfer pixel ownership.

The ABI1.3 capability16 surface_info/pixels_write candidate appears sufficient for synchronous dirty-rectangle replacement into the current drawing page: explicit format,x/y,width/height,stride/source_bytes; source consumed before return; whole validation before changes; pending Canvas work drained; no implicit swap/vblank. Reuse VDPL-005 rather than request another mode-specific blitter. FSIM would own module rendering and dirty regions; VDPlet owns any decision to promote its existing generic candidate. Conversion/copy cost and drain serialization may make it unsuitable for the present asynchronous aircraft pipeline.

No additional hook requested now. If future measurements justify asynchronous submission, first freeze a generic owned job contract: buffer-ID/offset+rectangle+destination+sequence input, job/status result, BUSY with no admission effects, retained storage references until explicit completion, and distinct copied/raster-complete/presented semantics. Never retain module pointers or code after return. This would require a separately selected design; today's buffer writes and ordinary bitmap drawing do not supply those ownership/completion guarantees.

Validation if dispatched: pixel equality for rectangle edges/stride/formats, unchanged clipping/palette and other graphics state, page ownership/cleanup, and end-to-end compose/present cost with near/far aircraft. RAM bounds and permanent firmware growth must be measured against the same baseline. The current candidate is not accepted/adopted by this return.

## Recommendation

Keep the current Pingo 2 asynchronous owner and current performance investigation. Do not attempt a wholesale Pingo VDPlet migration: one foreground slot, finite lifetimes and module memory/stack ceilings differ materially from the existing renderer. Document clock domains and completion types in any shared benchmark; reuse existing result buffers/counters rather than invent a new timing API. Consider FSIM-001/002 only when centrally selected; FSIM-003 is chiefly an existing-candidate/dependency review. No new implementation task or shared-source edit has been started.

returns.author: fsim-pingo
returns.body:
# Pingo VDPlet requirements and general asynchronous jobs

The Author explicitly asks this follow-up: send Pingo's specific VDPlet needs, beyond asynchronous rendering alone, and explain the value of asynchronous VDPlet operations to other applications. This expands the design discussion in my earlier return; it authorizes this note, not implementation, benchmark, firmware changes or deployment.

A loadable synchronous Pingo renderer is a credible first milestone. Async is a separate reusable runtime facility that could preserve our present overlap between rendering, command intake and presentation. It is not an inherent requirement of Pingo's rasterizer.

## 1. Context and measured size

Consumer: fsim-pingo, agon-fsim HEAD47b1a86758b03734abc04aad6cf99dd02029380f with owner work preserved. Continue unresolved FLIGHT-065/069 review/performance work; no supersession or new task start.

Upstream Pingo and the TurboVega render path are synchronous. Our worker/compositor wrapper was introduced October24 in FLIGHT-049; see PINGO-ENGINE-CHANGES.md N02/N05, ADR-0009 and utilities/corsair-backdrop-target/{README.md,scanout.h}. The current wrapper has one core1 render worker, two cropped aircraft output slots, immutable camera/status snapshots, and a separate compositor which copies to the hidden VGA page and uses stock vblank flips. Render completion, source-copy completion and visible presentation are distinct.

Read-only attribution from the retained current firmware.map: core .text14,200 + literals164 + rodata76 =14,440bytes; command owner adds .text16,554 + literals332 + rodata229 =17,115bytes, total31,555. These are mapped contributions, NOT a relocatable-module build or complete dependency/stack budget. Earlier matched production P023 over stock measured24,256flash bytes; the current entire firmware image is1,123,440bytes. Roughly46k over retained stock includes bridge/compositor/HUD/ground and must not be mistaken for the renderer alone or a newly matched build.

Thus the current32KiB default/64KiB ceiling for module text makes code fit plausible. Executable internal RAM availability, relocation/PIC/libm/libgcc growth, rodata/data accounting and whole-call-chain stack remain unqualified. Current worker reserves8192stack bytes; this is a reservation, not measured peak, but current VDPlet ceiling2048 must be investigated rather than presumed sufficient. Do not enlarge limits without evidence.

## 2. FSIM-004 — Specific loadable Pingo contract

1. **Native computation and scene inputs.** Preserve the selected Pingo2 C engine, perspective/clipping, depth testing, existing lighting and solid/textured materials. Application supplies meshes, indexed topology, UVs, material colors, textures, transforms, camera, viewport and output layout. Material-color rendering must work for untextured geometry; permit mixed solid/textured objects. Do not make Golem interpretation or per-triangle UART commands prerequisites. A compact operation/sequence/buffer descriptor can use existing32-byte RUN arguments; bulk inputs stay in ordinary buffers.

2. **Scoped storage with stable scene/work state.** Meshes, textures, color/depth targets and prepared state are much larger than module data limits and must be caller/runtime-owned PSRAM-capable storage, not embedded module globals. Preserve the four-lease limit for a synchronous prototype by packing offset-based scene/geometry and texture/work/output arenas as needed. Validate offsets/spans and reconstruct pointers during an invocation; never persist a buffer lease pointer after return. Current Pingo command owner uses a bridge allocator/resource registry not supplied by this ABI. Either build a smaller caller-provisioned arena adapter or propose bounded runtime-owned work-buffer allocation; do not assume firmware malloc/free imports or compiled firmware addresses. Cold scene preparation and reusable capacity should avoid hot-frame allocations.

3. **Offscreen output independent of presentation.** Need a caller-provided color target (current RGBA2222 bytes including transparency) plus depth/work storage, with explicit width/height/stride and capacity. Cropped model bounds and their screen origin should be returned with sequence/status/counters; retain a conservative near-plane fallback. Rendering must not implicitly clear the desktop, scroll or swap pages. FSIM's background/HUD/ground policy stays outside the engine.

4. **Installed bitmap integration.** Need a documented way to associate completed color storage with a host-created bitmap, or explicitly copy into its backing storage, then use stock bitmap drawing. Profile4 already draws installed bitmaps but does not establish that mutable-output association. Existing buffer mutation may suffice for a synchronous route if the bitmap's backing/layout/lifetime rules are documented and respected; otherwise the minimal missing hook is checked buffer-ID/offset-to-bitmap copy/publication, with format/stride/capacity validation and a defined copied/borrowed lifetime. Do not expose raw FabGL pointers. ABI1.3 pixels_write is an existing candidate for synchronous screen rectangles, but does not by itself provide an offscreen bitmap publication/lifetime contract, and its Canvas drain could serialize our pipeline.

5. **Discovery, lifecycle and errors.** Preserve older ABI views and optional capability checks. Reject malformed scenes, unavailable targets or insufficient storage explicitly; never claim successful output after a failed render. INIT/configure/prepare/render/status/retire can be module operation IDs without allocating them globally now. Drain jobs and bitmap copies before owner destruction, unload or buffer clearing. No need for runtime callbacks into arbitrary firmware or the entire legacy Pingo wire decoder in a first prototype.

6. **Minimum useful qualification if dispatched.** Core/module footprint and stack call-chain proof; exact or deliberately tolerance-bounded comparison of textured, flat and mixed scenes with existing firmware; cropped/near-plane/depth cases; repeated render/reset/release/failure checks; actual module buffer lifetimes; matched total frame and wire cost. Physical VGA/performance gates remain separate from Flexe. Current low wall-clock emulator rate has not been attributed to renderer/module overhead, so no speedup is promised.

## 3. FSIM-005 — General async job facility, not Pingo-specific firmware

User-visible benefit: a long native operation can proceed while the VDP command task continues accepting commands and the eZ80 works independently. It can also overlap compute with firmware-owned copying or presentation waits. It does not create extra CPU capacity, accelerate arithmetic by itself, or guarantee video/audio deadlines.

Proposed generic shape for owner assessment, not a frozen ABI:

- SUBMIT: module handle+generation, entry ID, caller sequence, a copied argument descriptor and explicit resource descriptors/access modes. Return a job handle/generation or BUSY/error. Runtime checks admission before retaining resources; queue capacity is bounded. A single compute worker with one running job and a small bounded pending/completion set would suffice for an initial Pingo assessment; simultaneous execution of multiple modules is not required.
- STATE/COLLECT: queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled plus module result, sequence and output metadata. Polling is sufficient initially; an optional notification must follow the established reply/event route and must not interfere with keyboard/controller packets. Completion remains observable until collected/retired.
- Runtime pins module code/data and explicit input/work/output resources until the job has stopped. Scoped worker leases last only for that worker invocation; foreground submit returning must NOT implicitly legitimize retaining today's expired pointers. Input mutations/clear/replace/free must be rejected, deferred or copy-on-submit by a documented policy; output remains unpublished until success.
- Default to serialized execution per module instance. Foreground RUN/INIT/FINI must not race worker globals or workspace; runtime status/cancel operations need not enter module code. Separate frame snapshots permit command intake to stage the next pose without mutating the worker's live scene.
- CANCEL may be queued-only or cooperative at documented checkpoints; unload/reset must drain a running job rather than forcibly freeing executable code or workspace. Do not promise safe preemption or cancellation of arbitrary native code. Native execution is trusted and remains capable of crashing firmware.
- Worker-safe services need an explicit allowlist. Pure math/buffer work is the first useful class. Today's VDU/Canvas/audio APIs must not be assumed thread-safe merely because RUN can be dispatched elsewhere. A worker may return an owned output descriptor for a foreground presentation owner to consume.
- Render DONE means output memory is ready. Bitmap-copy completion means output storage may be recycled. PRESENTED means page scanout has flipped. Preserve those separate fences. A completed first slot can be copied/presented while the second is rendering; vblank waiting must not unnecessarily hold the renderer.
- Runtime selects measured core/priority/scheduling and bounds queue/resource memory. Keep application algorithms in modules. Record queue wait, compute elapsed, copy/presentation counts and clock domains; guest ESP timing and host-wall presentation differ in Flexe. Physical timing is a separate qualification.

## 4. Broader consumers

1. Image decode, decompression, palette conversion and resizing: fill a prepared output buffer while command processing/UI continues.
2. Procedural graphics, terrain or texture generation: publish completed tiles without blocking unrelated display commands.
3. FFTs, signal analysis and other bounded numerical batches: process bulk data and return result buffers.
4. Physics, collision or pathfinding batches: submit a snapshot and later consume sequence-matched results; application owns stale-result policy and integration cadence.
5. Software emulation/block execution: finite slices can run in the worker and return state/output. No claim that an arbitrary endless emulator or its timing automatically fits.
6. Audio synthesis/mixing: compute future PCM chunks while firmware plays copied samples. Existing copied PCM already plays asynchronously after foreground RUN; the additional value here is nonblocking production. Audio deadlines need bounded scheduling and underrun policy, and a long Pingo job sharing one worker could make them worse.

These share job admission, retained resources, completion, bounded backpressure and safe retirement. They do not require a Pingo-shaped permanent renderer API, arbitrary background callbacks or unrestricted task creation by modules.

## 5. Ownership and recommendation

FSIM would own Pingo packaging, arenas/scene adapter, image correctness and consumer presentation. Golem/agon-vdplet would own any accepted generic async lifecycle, executable/storage admission, worker-safe service boundary and reusable bitmap storage contract. Consolidate pixels/publication with VDPL-005 and sound with the existing sink rather than duplicating services. Classic ESP32 only here; no promised Extender/P4 ABI.

Recommend assessing a synchronous Pingo module as a separable first milestone, then a bounded generic async worker to recover overlap if measured benefits justify it. Async is desirable and broadly reusable, not strictly necessary to prove loadable Pingo. This revises the earlier no-wholesale-migration caution into a concrete feasibility proposal; it is not a request to implement before the Author/Golem dispatch and contract freeze. Please include FSIM-004/005 with my earlier FSIM-001..003 in central GOLEM-056 review.

# Flexe return: existing services suffice; diagnose downstream audio delivery

Executive summary: the current VDPlet framework needs no new firmware service for Flexe's immediate work. Please consider dispatching the already-recorded FX-062 audio diagnostic before further audio integration is judged against emulator listening. Native-return, mixer-consumption, I2S delivery and host playback must remain separate observations. This return is consultation only; no implementation or new tests were performed.

Proposal FLEXE-AUD-001 — qualify audio delivery without expanding the VDPlet ABI.

1. Session/project and pins. Recipient identity flexe, existing chat flexe-agon-emulator, owned emulator HEAD a35b17d7dddb83d127ef4bb75f33a5808d9d8515 plus preserved working changes. Reviewed clean agon-vdplet 2541f10a1f8b06688bcecbc6d22eeae607da2b63 and the brief with SHA256 530b8ff2e8e00baad290372c5a572a3505a9a78175b7fd97d2256520765a5527. Current FX-062 is intake/proposed diagnosis, not released execution. Existing video/clock, quota and peer-owned CS0/SD25 work is not superseded. The Author's originating user turn in Golem was independently read to verify authority for this mailbox return.

2. Improvement and evidence. User-visible goal: faithful clean audio and note pacing from the unchanged stock and copied-PCM workloads. Existing Author listening distinguishes distorted stock Flexe from clean official Fab on identical client/bank/sample bytes. Underruns, I2S deadline drift and rate handling remain hypotheses/limitations, not a diagnosed cause. No new throughput, pitch or latency claim. The immediate deliverable should be a discriminating producer-versus-delivery capture, not another waveform/volume workaround.

3. Existing route. Ordinary stock notes and samples already fit VDU ABI1.1/capability 4 with profile 5 admission; AUDIO replies remain the success observation. Copied continuous PCM already has lean ABI1.5/capability 128 (module mask 129 with buffers; lean firmware mask 143), explicit priming, generation checks, whole-block BUSY backpressure and STATE counters. Audio code belongs in a finite C/C++ module; firmware retains only copied samples. No scheduler, retained native callback or second module slot is needed. Buffers 1, VDU 4 and lines 8, including current installed-bitmap/transform coverage, likewise need no emulator-specific service or host-native substitute for executed ESP32 work. The broader pixel/PCM/queue candidates are not required by this request.

4. Missing hook: emulator-local observation, no new firmware/wire API. The adapter currently ignores reported I2S rate, drops oldest samples on a full 65,536-sample ring and fills missing samples with 127; SDL declares a fixed 16,384-Hz source. A bounded host-owned diagnostic artifact should carry pre-ring PCM and bytes supplied to SDL, sequence/sample counts, declared format/rate, queue depth, produced/dequeued/missing/dropped counters, DMA deadline lateness, guest cycles and host monotonic timestamps. Label every boundary and incomplete/overflow capture explicitly; any copied payload is host-owned and never exposes a retained guest/native pointer. Capture limits/error reporting must not silently pass truncated evidence, and no diagnostic waiting may change guest backpressure. Sink STATE accepted/consumed/underrun counters describe the firmware ring/mixer; they cannot establish subsequent DMA, SDL or audible completion. Existing buffers cannot observe those later host boundaries.

There is also a specific rate-fidelity follow-up within this scope: copied PCM permits the current mixer to be changed to 24 kHz, whereas our current adapter discards the callback rate and the frontend declares 16,384 Hz. Respecting source-rate metadata belongs at the emulator adapter/frontend boundary. It is not a reason to change the module or firmware to a hard-coded workaround, and does not by itself explain the matched 16,384-Hz stock failure. A rate-transition/queue-epoch contract should be scoped only after measuring production/delivery, not invented as a new VDPlet ABI here.

5. Ownership/dependencies. Flexe owns optional instrumentation and any adapter/frontend correction under existing FX-062. A peripheral experiment must be a maintained patch to a generated export; vendor/flexe remains pinned/read-only. Golem/VDPlet owns the preserved controls, service/discovery semantics and any genuinely necessary generic documentation clarification. No Golem compiler change, new permanent firmware hook or parallel repair assignment is requested. Diagnose stock delivery first, then use copied-PCM STATE to distinguish module starvation from downstream loss. This duplicates an existing follow-up intentionally; please do not create a competing execution queue.

6. Validation and cost. After dispatch, use an owned Oryx copy of the frozen stock fixture and retained Fab reference, with identical client/bank/sample, levels, envelopes and note pacing. Compare contiguous raw waveform and delivery gaps, rates per guest second versus per host second, and DMA lateness; identify actual SDL capture format before waveform analysis. Later cover copied PCM at discovered default and 24 kHz, saturation/underrun/flush/close and rate changes, with human listening and existing keyboard/video checks. Those are proposed gates, not tests run for this consultation. Permanent firmware/static-RAM/new wire cost proposed: zero. Host diagnostic storage and execution overhead need explicit bounds and measurement; any later correction's resource cost remains unknown.

7. Recommendation. Now: jointly review/dispatch the bounded FX-062 diagnostic, already covered by our issue log. Later: qualify rate handling and copied-PCM delivery using the existing API, with no inferred hardware claim. Existing FX-032 also tracks MOS time tied to native-frame production and an exported correction; its frontend port is a separate timing dependency worth coordinating before using MOS ticks as calibrated audio time, not a request for a firmware clock service. No additional VDPlet feature is useful from this emulator's perspective until a missing boundary is demonstrated. Preserve INFO capability/size/null checks, completion semantics and the human listening gate.

This invitation authorizes only this analysis/response. No emulator/benchmark, build, firmware/profile change, implementation, hardware action or commit/push was performed. Existing source and pending work were preserved.

# MODEL-001 — Modeler capability consultation: no new firmware hook requested

Session: fsim 3d modeler, 01a1477c-09c1-7951-97df-217d4342b776; project /Agon/mystuff/agon-fsim; current published dev pin47b1a86758b03734abc04aad6cf99dd02029380f. MODEL-045 is already in progress: offline measured NACA0012-wing comparison with existing flow5 viscous coupling. It continues unchanged. The consultation is analysis/response only; no new tests, implementation or deployment were performed for it.

Read the invited capability brief (SHA530b8ff2e8e00baad290372c5a572a3505a9a78175b7fd97d2256520765a5527), pinned public C ABI/start guide at agon-vdplet2541f10a1f8b06688bcecbc6d22eeae607da2b63, and fsim ADR-0004/renderer lineage/change ledger. Independently verified direct Author approval in Golem user message01a18eb2-b17b-7ad1-a011-266ea361afec: Approve all consultation replies. This reply does not claim an implementation assignment.

Improvement/disposition: no useful new permanent firmware feature for current model authoring or aerodynamic analysis. Geometry, UVs, textures and aero lookup tables are generated offline. Keeping their computation offline avoids adding per-tick work on the eZ80. No measured runtime bottleneck from this session establishes a need to move aerodynamic lookup or geometry preparation to a VDPlet. Renderer/frame pacing is owned by fsim-pingo, whose separate return should govern that scope.

Existing route: future asset consumers can use ordinary VDP buffers and existing scoped native buffer acquire/release; the public ABI supports module-owned arithmetic. Bulk tables/meshes belong in host-owned buffers, with small invocation arguments. A module must release leases before return and reacquire on later calls; do not retain buffer pointers. Native line batches already cover a possible wireframe preview, and installed-bitmap VDU submission covers resident 2D asset drawing, subject to actual capability/coverage discovery. These are consumer/module choices, not a request to expand firmware. This does not promise textured 3D rendering through the installed-bitmap service. The classic ESP32 ABI is not an Extender/P4 ABI commitment.

Missing hook: none identified for current work. No request for a mesh loader, aerodynamic solver, aircraft-specific draw call, persistent callback, asynchronous module job, or new permanent rendering service. Candidate generic-colour and queued-audio facilities are not prerequisites here. Retain ADR-0004's accepted Pingo2 ownership/boundary and existing Extender/P4 gates.

Ownership/dependencies: modeler owns offline asset/solver inputs and validation; runtime mesh/texture ingestion and renderer lifecycle/performance remain the fsim owner’s work. No changes requested of Golem or agon-vdplet. Do not duplicate or override fsim-pingo's proposals; any future asset-format handoff should join its accepted task rather than creating a parallel firmware contract.

Validation/cost if a later consumer is selected: compare a tiny pinned mesh/texture/table payload through existing buffer services, verify decoded values/UVs and output against the host reference, then measure target frame cost, wire bytes and actual memory. This is a possible future acceptance shape, not a released test. Present proposal requires zero additional firmware bytes/services; future module/RAM/wire cost is unmeasured and must be qualified by its owner.

Recommendation: already covered/no implementation now. Continue current offline aero validation, leave production adoption and renderer work under their existing task gates, and reconsider only with a concrete consumer bottleneck or missing operation.

# Wireframe consultation return — WIRE-001

The current handwritten C++ wireframe already fits the public buffer/native-line ABI. No new firmware service is requested. Drawing dominates the measured workload; direct perspective division is inexpensive. Broader scene/rendering algorithms should stay optional module code rather than become permanent firmware solely for this experiment.

1. Session/project and pins. Established identity fsim-wireframe, Explore stock VDP wireframe, agon-fsim. TEST-009 complete handwritten C++ worker and TEST-011 polygon-aware backface culling are qualified/delivered; Author visual gates remain open. TEST-011's current task records the separate 2026-10-28 publication release; do not treat old pending-publication paragraphs as its current publication state. Existing consumer SDK pin c4ed7574787768251c882954edb10231b2782cbf, generic firmware SHA256 211a81d2b28836b2e0da80d9c387673c37ef7fb0acad4ff0d1b67f6fa0bc433a. This review read current SDK HEAD 2541f10a1f8b06688bcecbc6d22eeae607da2b63 and its API/coverage references; no consumer upgrade or new qualification is implied. No existing project work is superseded.

2. Improvement/evidence. TEST-011 same-module/image/backend reverse-order Oryx actual-Xtensa comparisons (144 measured frames per arm) give uncull/cull throughput 5.048/9.152 FPS orthographic and 5.054/9.223 FPS perspective. Culling preserves an original edge whenever ANY incident original polygon is front-facing, keeps loose edges and does not introduce triangle diagonals. Separate fenced phase samples show drawing roughly 193 ->101ms while transform/cull costs roughly 4–7ms. Those phase medians have extra fences and are not additive decompositions of whole-frame medians. Thus keeping unnecessary lines out of the rasterizer is demonstrably useful; further public matrix/division services are not needed by this worker. Earlier TEST-008 same-image comparison also found native direct perspective 0.532751s/frame vs stock orthographic 0.533037s, against native generic inverse 1.477153s. All are scoped emulator measurements, not physical FPS or universal ratios. The earlier ~10.6x stock-perspective/native comparison changes both projection and drawing submission, and must not be advertised as a division-only speedup.

3. Existing route. Capability mask9 (buffers1 + native lines8), ABI1.2, suffices. The module directly performs matrix/projection/culling/edge loops in native Xtensa C++, then submits batches of32 endpoints through draw_lines. There is no Golem-generated intermediate, buffered-command interpreter in those hot loops, per-vertex eZ80 work or runtime transformed-vertex download. Host preparation/upload is separate. Four leases work by copying scalar arguments and releasing their lease before acquiring source/topology/scratch/result spans; no pointers survive return and no RUN heap allocation occurs. The newer base feature build (mask15) should cover the required services; that is API coverage assessment, not a new firmware adoption test. No PCM, generic color-rectangle candidate or scheduled-audio service is required. New ordinary VDU coverage could optionally move existing HUD/clear submissions into a module, but would not remove raster cost and has no demonstrated performance benefit here.

4. Missing hook. None for the demonstrated bounded wireframe. General near-plane/frustum clipping and true hidden-line/depth removal are absent application algorithms, not evidence of a missing buffer API. They can be designed inside an optional module if the Author selects them. Do not add a permanent scene renderer, arbitrary framebuffer pointer, async callback or renderer-specific ABI on this consumer's behalf. Native return is submission completion only; current C3 plus ordered GP application fence remains required before resource teardown or completed-frame timing. New bitmap coverage does not by itself turn a wireframe module into a solid renderer or replace Pingo.

5. Ownership/dependencies. fsim-wireframe retains utilities/cpp-wireframe and utilities/cpp-wireframe-cull, their fixtures, scalar client, numerical/topology contracts and Oryx review artifacts. Golem/agon-vdplet owns compiler/runtime/public ABI. fsim-pingo owns the selected production Pingo architecture and its independent experiments; this response does not request changes there or a Pingo replacement. No shared source edits, emulator use or assigned successor is requested. There is no new implementation task to duplicate TEST-009/011.

6. Validation/cost if a later SDK migration is authorized. Reuse the existing pinned Corsair poses, coordinate/raster/face-edge oracle, invalid-input/recovery/reload tests, actual MOS lifecycle and matched completed-frame timing. Require old module load/run compatibility, optional-capability/table-extent checks and unchanged drawing semantics/fences. Keep geometry, logical coordinates, backend, console/capture policy and frame boundaries fixed. Current worker package is8192bytes, topology133568bytes, scratch39384bytes in host-owned VDP buffers; retained actual-target minimum free command stack2180bytes. Those are current measurements, not a forecast for a new image. Requested permanent firmware/RAM/wire increment: zero. Cost of any future migration remains unmeasured. Human visual review and physical qualification remain distinct.

7. Recommendation — WIRE-001: already covered / no useful additional hook now. Retain the lean buffer-plus-native-lines route and existing completed work. Treat compiler optimization, more visibility/clipping or a solid native module as separately scoped future choices requiring Author dispatch, not work released by this consultation. No implementation, test, emulator launch, deployment, commit or benchmark was performed for this return.
